sourceGuide.title: The Ayahs of the Qur’an – Muhkam and Mutashabih
sourceGuide.method: Ashari-Maturidi Sunni muhkam/mutashabih guidance with the project-owner guide as the operative verse-level source

editorialPrinciples: Muhkam verses govern the interpretation of mutashabih wording.
No English wording may attribute bodily, spatial, directional, created, sensuous or human modality to Allah.
Salaf-style tafwid with tanzih and contextual Khalaf-style tawil are both supported where the supplied guide supports them.
The Ashari and Maturidi traditions share the governing tanzih principle used by this project; verse-specific wording remains traceable to the project guide or a recorded contextual review.
A verse-specific tawil must not be turned into a universal lexical substitution rule.
All verses in the full-corpus attribute-risk inventory must have an explicit SalahOS 2026 treatment; phrase rewrites fail closed if the pinned Pickthall wording changes.

baseRewrites.to: Then He directed His will to the heaven

entries.editorialNote: Full-corpus audit: Occurrences of istawa ila al-sama that must not be rendered as bodily turning or movement. The SalahOS 2026 layer changes only the creed-sensitive Pickthall phrase(s) recorded for this verse and leaves the remaining baseline wording intact.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while categorically denying bodily, spatial, directional, created or human modality and without assigning a created 'how'.
entries.khalafReading: Apply the recorded contextual ta'wil to this verse only, in accordance with Arabic context and the governing tanzih foundations; do not turn it into a universal lexical substitution.

entries.englishMeaning: To Allah belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the qiblah appointed by Allah. Surely Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide reports Mujahid's explanation of wajh in this verse as qiblah, in the context of voluntary prayer while travelling. SalahOS does not render the expression as a bodily face of Allah.
entries.salafReading: The verse is understood without attributing a face, direction or location to Allah.
entries.khalafReading: Mujahid is cited in the supplied guide as explaining wajh here as qiblah, the direction of prayer in its context.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: Qiblah, the direction of prayers during voluntary prayer while travelling.

entries.englishMeaning: And when We made the House, the Ka'bah, a house greatly honoured by Allah, a place of return for people and a place of safety: take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer. We commanded Ibrahim and Ismail: Purify My House for those who perform tawaf, remain there in worship, bow and prostrate.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide explicitly rejects reading 'My House' as Allah's residence. It gives the meaning that the Ka'bah is a house of great honour to Allah.
entries.salafReading: The possessive attribution is understood as one of honour and not residence, containment or place for Allah.
entries.khalafReading: The guide gives the specific meaning: the Ka'bah is a house of great honour to Allah.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: The Ka'bah is a house of a great honor to Allah.

entries.editorialNote: Full-corpus audit: Fi al-sama wording must not place Allah inside the sky; render supreme status/dominion without location. The SalahOS 2026 layer changes only the creed-sensitive Pickthall phrase(s) recorded for this verse and leaves the remaining baseline wording intact.
entries.salafReading: Affirm the revealed wording according to a meaning befitting Allah while categorically denying bodily, spatial, directional, created or human modality and without assigning a created 'how'.

entries.englishMeaning: On the Day of anguish and hardship, they will be called to prostrate, but they will not be able.
entries.editorialNote: The supplied guide reports the explanation of saq as hardship and the verse as referring to a day of anguish and hardship; it attributes this explanation to Ibn Abbas and other early scholars.
entries.salafReading: The supplied guide records early Salaf authorities explaining the expression without attributing a bodily shin to Allah.
entries.khalafReading: Saq is explained contextually as hardship or severe anguish.
entries.guideSpecificMeaning: A day of anguish and hardship.

entries.englishMeaning: And an indication of your Lord's Power comes, and the angels, rank upon rank.
